sections.h2: Where is Aiken, South Carolina, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Aiken is the county seat and largest city of Aiken County, about 20 miles northeast of Augusta, Georgia. US 1 and US 78 run through town, and Interstate 20 passes about 6 miles to the north, reached by SC Highway 19 at exit 18 or US 1 at exit 22.

The city covers 21.58 square miles. The 2020 census counted 32,025 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 33,808. The median age was 47.6, and 29.3 percent of residents were 65 or older.

An older population means estate sales and downsizing moves are a normal part of the local picture, and both can leave a house to sell with a tight timeline.

sections.h2: What is Aiken's history, and why does it still matter for houses?
sections.html:
Aiken was incorporated on December 19, 1835, around the end of a rail line running from Charleston to the Savannah River. It is named for William Aiken, the first president of that railroad.

In the late 1800s wealthy families from the Northeast began spending winters here, and Thomas Hitchcock Sr. and William C. Whitney helped found the Aiken Winter Colony. That legacy explains the horse culture. The Aiken Training Track, the Aiken Thoroughbred Racing Hall of Fame and Museum (founded 1977) and the Aiken Steeplechase Association (founded 1930) are all part of town life. The Imperial Cup runs in March and the Holiday Cup in October.

It also explains the older housing stock. Hopelands Gardens and the roughly 2,100 acres of Hitchcock Woods sit inside the city, and older homes around them may fall under the exterior review rules described below.

The Savannah River Site is the biggest single influence. The Atomic Energy Commission announced the site near Aiken on November 30, 1950, and it was renamed the Savannah River Site in 1989. Savannah River Nuclear Solutions, a Fluor and HII partnership, manages and operates it.

The Department of Energy's second quarter report for fiscal year 2025 shows where site employees live. It excludes NNSA and some subcontractors, so it undercounts the full workforce.

The site also trains its own workers. Its page reports 29 registered apprenticeships, more than 800 apprentices graduated since the program went sitewide in 2020, and 91 percent of graduates placed in full-time site jobs. A job change at a site this large can also leave a household with a house to sell on a short clock.

sections.h2: How do Aiken's weather and roads affect an older house?
sections.html:
Aiken has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and cool, dry winters, and it is milder than much of the state. Rainfall averages about 51 inches a year, and snow averages only about half an inch. The record high is 109 degrees (August 21, 1983) and the record low is minus 4 degrees (January 21, 1985).

With that much rain and heat, roofs, crawl spaces and cooling systems tend to draw attention on an older house. A buyer's inspector will look at roofs, crawl spaces, HVAC age and moisture, and a long repair list can slow a conventional sale.

Public schools are part of the Aiken County Public School District, and the city's high schools include Aiken High, South Aiken High and Silver Bluff High.

sections.h2: Does Aiken have historic district rules that affect a seller?
sections.html:
Yes, if your address is in a review area. Aiken's Design Review Board reviews Certificate of Appropriateness applications, and the city sets two filing deadlines.

  • Complex projects need an application 30 days before the board meets. That covers new construction, demolition, additions, relocations, porch enclosures and work touching more than one exterior historic feature.
  • Simpler projects need an application 14 days before a meeting. That list includes non-in-kind window, door or siding replacement, fences, gutters, handicap ramps, painting, paving and screening a porch.

If you plan to renovate before listing, the review calendar can add weeks. If you sell as-is, the buyer inherits the question, so the seller does not wait on it.

sections.h2: What does South Carolina require when you sell an Aiken house?
sections.html:
Most sellers of a one to four unit home must hand the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. It covers water and sewer, structure, mechanical systems, wood-destroying insects, zoning, environmental hazards such as lead paint and radon, leases and homeowners association rules.

Some transfers are excluded from the disclosure rule.

  • Court-ordered transfers and foreclosure-related transfers.
  • Transfers by a fiduciary, such as an estate representative.
  • Transfers to a spouse or lineal relative.
  • Sales where both sides agree in writing not to complete the form.

State law also allows an as-is agreement, and it says the buyer remains responsible for inspecting the property. A seller who knowingly gives false or incomplete information can be liable for actual damages and court costs.

The closing is overseen by a South Carolina attorney, because the State Bar treats every stage of a real estate transaction as the practice of law. The attorney prepares the deed, runs the title work and records the deed in the Aiken County Register of Deeds office.

sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Deeds for Aiken property are recorded at the Aiken County Register of Deeds, in the Government Center at 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100. The phone is 803-642-2072.

The office keeps records back to 1872. Documents recorded after June 12, 2005 are imaged and can be viewed on computers in the office, and earlier documents are kept in book form. The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of the price, and the county retains $0.55 of each $1.85.

The county page does not list a fee table, so ask the office or your closing attorney for the full recording total on your deed.

sections.h2: How does property tax work when you sell in Aiken?
sections.html:
Aiken County property tax is billed once a year, and state law sets the calendar. Taxes are payable from September 30 through January 15. Late penalties then step up: 3 percent from January 16, 7 percent more after the second of February, and 5 percent more after March 17.

An owner-occupied home is assessed at 4 percent of value if the owner applied for the legal residence rating, and other residential property is assessed at 6 percent. A sale is a reappraisal event, so the buyer's bill can differ from yours.

Sellers who are 65 or older, disabled or legally blind may already have the state homestead exemption of the first $50,000 of value. For the Aiken County assessor and treasurer details, see our Aiken County property tax guide.

faqs.q: How many people live in Aiken, SC?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 32,025 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 33,808. Aiken is the most populous city in Aiken County.

faqs.q: Do I need to disclose problems when I sell my Aiken house?
faqs.a: Usually yes. South Carolina requires a written disclosure statement for most sales of one to four unit homes, with listed exceptions such as fiduciary and foreclosure transfers. An as-is sale is allowed, but a false statement can still create liability.

faqs.q: Does Aiken have a historic district review for exterior changes?
faqs.a: Yes. The Design Review Board reviews Certificate of Appropriateness applications, with filing deadlines of 30 days for complex projects and 14 days for simpler ones before a meeting.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Aiken?
faqs.a: At the Aiken County Register of Deeds, 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100. Call 803-642-2072 to confirm requirements. Your closing attorney normally handles the recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Aiken house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. South Carolina law allows as-is sales, and you can sell without fixing anything. Disclosure rules and any open code or tax liens still apply.
